{"idea":"The defining equation forces each element of S to be either 8 or -14, so S has at most two elements. Both values satisfy the equation, and the finite sum is their sum, -6.","proof":"have hmem (x : ℝ) : x ∈ S ↔ x = 8 ∨ x = -14 := by
  rw [h₀ x]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h' : (x + 3 - 11) * (x + 3 + 11) = 0 := by nlinarith [h]
    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h' with h' | h'
    · left
      linarith
    · right
      linarith
  · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> norm_num
have hS : S = {8, -14} := by
  ext x
  rw [hmem]
  simp
rw [hS]
simp
